{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan cuisine]]

'''Wheat grass juice''' is the extracted juice from young (5–10 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]] plants. The juice is touted for many health benefits due to its high concentrations of Chlorophyll, enzymes, vitamins (especially vitamin B), and minerals.  

A typical portion is two fluid ounces, requiring the juicing of ⅓ to 1 square foot of wheat grass. The juice has a pungent, sweet odor/taste which is an acquired taste. It may be drunk straight, or mixed with other juices, such as carrot or apple.

Wheatgrass juice should always be consumed immediately after juicing.

==Ingredients==
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]] berries

== Equipment ==
* 1 tray (cafeteria type, to grow shoots on)
* 2 cups potting soil
* Large jar

== Procedure ==
[[Image:WheatGrass.jpg|thumb|right|280px|1 week-old wheat grass]]

=== Growing ===
# Soak the wheat berries overnight in a jar of water.
# Drain, then cover with damp [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]] and keep in the jar. Let rest for a day or so until they have sprouted.
# Spread the potting soil on the tray, and then gently spread the sprouts on top.
# Regularly water the sprouts for about a week, or until they are plentiful enough to juice. This should take about 1 week.

=== Juicing ===
#Use an electric or manual juicer to juice the wheat grass.
#Use immediately.
